subject: Post-demo: Performance & SLO recap / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rajesh Singh <rajesh@fintechco.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Performance & SLO recap / next steps

Thanks again for your time today — great discussion. Per our demo, below is a concise recap of the performance/SLO items we covered and proposed next steps (POC/MAP). Please read and confirm anything you want changed.

Quick recap of performance asks you called out during the call:
- Latency: target P95 for interactive requests (streaming responses) — 300ms target for ~256-token responses; fallback acceptable up to 450ms for longer sequences.
- Throughput & concurrency: want sustained throughput of ~150-200 req/s with bursts to 400 req/s during market opens; concurrency target 80-100 concurrent streaming connections.
- Streaming: essential — client-side wants token-by-token stream (low tail latency).
- Availability & fallback: regional routing + model variant fallback preferred for graceful degradation.

SLO checklist (attached 20260302-slo_checklist.pdf):
- Measurable metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, errors/sec, stream drop rate.
- Test harness: we will provide a perf harness and synthetic traffic profile matching your production token distributions.
- Success criteria for POC: sustained P95 <= 350ms under your baseline 200 req/s, streaming intact, no >1% stream drop.

Proposed next steps / MAP items:
1) Confirm test window and sample workload (we propose Tue 3/9 or Wed 3/10 09:00-12:00 PT).
2) Redwood to deliver perf harness, baseline config, and a test plan (assigned: Dev Patel).
3) FintechCo to provide a short representative prompt corpus and expected token distribution.
4) Agree POC timeline and reporting cadence; define stakeholder owners.

Attachments: demo-recording-20260302.mp4, 20260302-slo_checklist.pdf
Links: HubSpot deal and MAP doc (see related_links).

Thanks — I'll coordinate scheduling once you confirm the test window.

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0182
From: Rajesh Singh <rajesh@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@fintechco.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 17:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance & SLO recap / next steps

Thanks, Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side before we lock the POC window:
1) Latency: for our most latency-sensitive routes (market-data summarization) we need P95 <= 300ms for ~256 tokens while streaming. If you can achieve 350ms in the POC that's promising, but we need a clear path to 300ms in production.
2) Concurrency: during open hours we can see 100-120 concurrent streaming users. Can Redwood sustain that concurrency with your proposed batching/caching without increasing tail latency?
3) Model variants & fallback: if the primary model can't meet the SLOs under load, what's the automated fallback behavior and how do you ensure output quality?
4) Compliance: please include SOC 2 evidence and any logging/audit capabilities we can show our security team.

Assuming we get clear answers on the above we are prepared to proceed to a 2-week POC. We'd like a short technical kickoff with Dev (your engineering contact) to align on the harness.

Regards,
Rajesh Singh
Head of Infrastructure | FintechCo
rajesh@fintechco.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rajesh Singh <rajesh@fintechco.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance & SLO recap / next steps

Great questions — addressing each below and calling out owners:

1) Latency path to 300ms (owner: Rishi) — We can target P95 350ms in the POC with the following levers to reach 300ms in production: quantized model variant, optimized kernels, and tuned continuous-batching for streaming. Rishi, I asked the runtime team to prepare a short plan on kernel selection and quantization choices for the 256-token profile.

2) Concurrency (owner: Dev) — Redwood's serving runtime supports 100+ concurrent streaming connections; in the POC we will stress test to 120 concurrent streams and provide results. Dev will run a configuration sweep (batch sizes, KV cache sizing, and autoscale thresholds) during the test.

3) Fallback behavior (owner: Marissa/Rishi) — Our routing policy will route to a lower-cost/less-latency-optimized variant or a nearby region if the primary variant misses SLOs. We'll provide a quality regression report between variants; we can also configure A/B fallback with acceptance thresholds.

4) Compliance & logs (owner: Priyom) — attaching SOC 2 summary and logging capabilities; we'll surface audit log retention options and how logs can be forwarded to your SIEM.

POC plan (high level):
- Duration: 2 weeks.
- Success criteria: P95 <= 350ms under your baseline; evidence of path to 300ms; concurrency validated up to 120 streams; streaming stability <1% drop.
- Deliverables: perf report, recording, kernel/quantization recommendations, MAP with next steps and estimated Dedicated sizing.

Proposed kickoff: Thu 3/5 10:00 PT for a 45-min technical kickoff with Dev and Rishi. Does that work?

Marissa
